name: Sure As Ship for WooCommerce
author: sureasship

sections.description:
Sure As Ship for WooCommerce connects your store to Sure As Ship, a Canadian shipping platform. Your customers see live commercial rates from Canada Post, FedEx, UPS and Purolator at checkout, and you book labels without leaving WooCommerce.

Features

  • Live rates at checkout from the carriers you choose, in both the classic and block checkout
  • Pass your discounted rate on to customers, or show retail and keep the difference
  • Markup percentage and flat handling fee
  • Book the service the customer picked with one click, or automatically in the background when an order reaches Processing or Completed
  • Book orders placed with any other shipping method from the order screen
  • Download labels; Canada Post QR codes for printing at a post office
  • Return labels and Canada Post return QR codes
  • Tracking number added to the order, the customer’s order page and their emails
  • Where each parcel is (Delivered, In transit, Out for delivery…) and its carrier scans on the order screen, with a Refresh tracking button
  • Several ship-from locations, chosen per order
  • Optional box packing into the box sizes you use
  • Customs information for cross-border shipments, with per-product HS codes
  • Signature, Saturday delivery and hold-for-pickup options, and scheduled carrier pickups

What you need

  • A Sure As Ship account and an API key from it
  • A ship-from address in Canada, or in the US for US-registered accounts
  • Shipments are billed by Sure As Ship to your account. The plugin itself is free. A test API key books sandbox labels that are never charged, so you can try everything first.

External services

This plugin needs the Sure As Ship API (https://sureasship.com/api/ecommerce/v1), operated by Sure As Ship, to work. Nothing is sent until you save an API key, and nothing is sent that is not needed for the action below.

  • At checkout and on the cart page, to show rates: the ship-from postal code, province and country; the destination street address (once the shopper has entered it), postal code, city, province, country and company name; the weight and dimensions of each item in the cart; and your rate settings (carriers, packing method and boxes, delivery options). For a destination outside the ship-from country, each cart item’s name, price, quantity, weight, HS code, country of manufacture, SKU and product page link is also sent, with its manufacturer part number, barcode and U.S. customs answers when you have entered them, so prepaid US and EU duties can be estimated. The street lets carriers such as UPS tell a business address from a home and price it the way they will bill it. No customer name, email or phone number is sent to get rates.
  • When a shipment is booked (by you, or automatically if you turn that on): the ship-from address, phone and store admin email; the customer’s name, company, shipping address, phone and email, which the carrier needs for the label; item weights and dimensions; your order ID as a reference; and, for cross-border shipments, each item’s name, value, quantity, weight, HS code, country of manufacture, SKU and product page link, with its manufacturer part number, barcode and U.S. customs answers when you have entered them.
  • When you test the connection, save settings, or open an order: your API key, to read your account’s name, billing status and allowed ship-from countries, and the order’s labels, customs documents, and each shipment’s status and carrier scans.
  • When you create a return, void a shipment, download a label or click Refresh tracking: the Sure As Ship shipment or return ID. Refresh tracking asks Sure As Ship to check with the carrier now.

Sure As Ship passes shipment details to the carrier you choose (Canada Post, FedEx, UPS or Purolator) so it can carry the parcel.

  • Sure As Ship terms of service: https://sureasship.com/terms
  • Sure As Ship privacy policy: https://sureasship.com/privacy

Tracking links in the order screen and customer emails point to the carrier’s own tracking page (canadapost-postescanada.ca, fedex.com, ups.com or purolator.com); they are only visited when someone clicks them.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Sure As Ship”, then install and activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. Sign in at sureasship.com and create an API key under API Keys. Use a test key first if you like.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Sure As Ship. Paste the key, click Test Connection, check your ship-from location, choose carriers, and save.
  4. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Shipping zones, edit a zone (for example “Canada”), click “Add shipping method” and choose “Sure As Ship”.

Customers in that zone now see live rates at checkout.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Sure As Ship account?

Yes. Rates and labels come from your Sure As Ship account, and shipments are billed to it. Sign up at sureasship.com.

Which carriers are supported?

Canada Post, FedEx, UPS and Purolator. Choose which ones to quote under Enabled Carriers.

Does it work with the block checkout?

Yes. Rates appear in both the Cart and Checkout blocks and the classic checkout.

Can I test without being charged?

Yes. Create a test API key (it starts with sas_test_). Rates are real, but bookings use carrier sandboxes and are never charged.

What happens if Sure As Ship can’t be reached?

If you enable the fallback, customers see the flat rate you set. The same applies if Sure As Ship cannot quote for your account (it is suspended, or it is BYOC-only with no carrier account set up), and an admin notice tells you why. You then book those orders from the order screen with “Book with Sure As Ship”. If a destination or cart cannot be shipped at all, no Sure As Ship rate is shown.

What if a product has no dimensions or weight?

The default dimensions (12x8x6 in) and weight (0.5 lb) in the settings are used. Add real dimensions to your products for accurate rates.

Can I ship orders that used flat rate or free shipping?

Yes. Open the order and click “Book with Sure As Ship” to see live rates and pick a service.

Is shipping taxed?

Each Sure As Ship shipping method in a zone has its own Tax Status setting, like any WooCommerce shipping method. Prepaid duties are never taxed as shipping: they are their own line beside it, such as “US duties & taxes”.

Does it work with WooPayments Multi-Currency?

Yes. A shopper who picks another currency sees Sure As Ship rates converted from your store’s currency, like your other shipping rates, and customs values are declared in your store’s currency.

How do I get my products ready for customs?

Answer the customs questions on each product’s Shipping tab, then choose “Send all products to Sure As Ship” under WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Sure As Ship (International Shipping). Every product goes to your Sure As Ship product catalog at once, and the page lists each product that still needs an answer, with a link to it. Fix those, then choose “Send these again”.

I installed an earlier version from sureasship.com. How do I switch?

Install this plugin and activate it. It switches the old copy off automatically, and your settings, orders and shipments carry over. Then delete the old copy (it is listed as “Sure As Ship for WooCommerce” with version 1.x).
sections.changelog:
2.0.18

  • New: Prepaid duties are their own line at checkout and on the order, beside shipping (“US duties & taxes”, or “EU duties & VAT” on Canada Post parcels to the EU). A store that charges tax on shipping no longer taxes the duties. The line follows the shipping option and the address the shopper picks, and is converted for shoppers who pick another currency with WooPayments Multi-Currency. Each option says the duty is added, for example “(+ US duties & taxes)”, and options are still listed by what the shopper pays in all. Your markup and handling fee still apply to shipping only
  • Changed: UPS Standard’s customs brokerage stays in its shipping price, as the faster UPS services include it in theirs, so UPS options compare like for like

2.0.17

  • New: “Send all products to Sure As Ship” in the International Shipping settings. It sends every product’s customs answers (HS code, country of manufacture, CUSMA, steel and aluminum, the U.S. agency categories, part number and barcode) to your Sure As Ship product catalog at once, so a CUSMA claim on Canada Post parcels to the U.S. can be set up before a product’s first parcel. The page then lists each product that still needs an answer, in Sure As Ship’s own words, with a link to edit it, and “Send these again” sends just those. Only each product’s own answers are sent, not the store-wide defaults
  • Fix: Shoppers who pick another currency with WooPayments Multi-Currency now see Sure As Ship rates, converted from your store’s currency like your other shipping rates. Before, they saw none, even for a local address, and the store showed a false currency-mismatch notice
  • Fix: For those orders, customs values are declared in your store’s currency, at the exchange rate WooPayments recorded on the order, so cross-border bookings are no longer refused for their currency
  • Fix: A booking Sure As Ship says is booked at the carrier but not paid or not confirmed is no longer retried by auto-booking. The order note gives Sure As Ship’s own words, which say to contact support, and the shipment number when there is one
  • Fix: A refused return label or return QR code says why in Sure As Ship’s own words, without “API error” in front
  • Fix: When Sure As Ship is briefly too busy to answer (too many requests in a minute), checkout shows your fallback rate instead of no Sure As Ship option, and auto-booking tries again a few minutes later instead of giving up

2.0.16

  • New: From November 4, 2026, Sure As Ship prepays EU duties and VAT on Canada Post parcels to Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia, Spain and Sweden. Those rates read “(includes EU duties & VAT)” at checkout, and U.S. rates still read “(includes US duties & taxes)”
  • New: “Manufacturer part or model number” on each product’s Shipping tab. EU customs asks for product identifiers from November 1, 2026, so each item’s part or model number and its GTIN, UPC, EAN or ISBN barcode are now sent with cross-border quotes and shipments, beside the SKU, which Sure As Ship uses when the part number is blank. A barcode with a wrong check digit is not sent
  • Fix: A booking refused for missing or wrong EU product identifiers says what is wrong, in Sure As Ship’s own words, and where to fix it in WooCommerce
  • Changed: The missing-HS-code notice now also covers Canada Post orders to the EU, which are quoted without prepaid duties until every product has an HS code

2.0.15

  • New: “Orders at Your Own Rates” (off by default). With auto-booking on, an order placed at one of your own shipping rates (such as Free shipping or Flat rate), or at the fallback rate, is booked with the cheapest tracked service that can take it, and an order note says which service and why. Local pickup orders are never booked. For these orders the Book dialog opens on that service
  • New: Void Shipment says how much credit went back to your Sure As Ship account, and why it is less than the charge when it is
  • Fix: Book Shipment never charges more than the price the dialog showed. If the price has gone up since, nothing is booked, you are told the new price, and the dialog shows today’s prices so you can book at the new one
  • Fix: Quotes at checkout and on the order screen include the delivery street, so UPS prices a business address as a business, the same as the booking is charged
  • Fix: U.S. rates whose duties cannot be prepaid (goods under an anti-dumping or countervailing duty order, or an import quota) are no longer offered at checkout, and a notice names the products
  • Fix: A booking or return refused for your Sure As Ship billing (such as a prepaid card on file, which Sure As Ship does not accept) or for the new-account shipment limit now says why in Sure As Ship’s own words, in the Book dialog, the order notes and the auto-booking notice
  • Changed: “Default Incoterm” now starts as “Use my Sure As Ship company setting” instead of DAP, so your company’s own setting applies. A term you already chose is kept
  • Changed: A new ship-from location starts as a residential address, so the carrier’s residential pickup charge is never under-quoted. Untick it for a business address. Saved locations keep their setting

2.0.14

  • New: When your Sure As Ship account credit (from a voided shipment or a refund) pays for some or all of a shipment, the order screen shows the credit applied and the amount paid by card under the shipment cost, and an order note says the same

2.0.13

  • New: U.S. customs details on each product’s Shipping tab, for parcels to the U.S. from October 22, 2026: the product’s steel and aluminum (percent of the product and the countries it was melted, smelted or cast in, for Section 232 duties), whether it is food, cosmetics, supplements, medicine, pet products, a children’s product, wood or plant products, or animal materials, and whether it is made in Canada and qualifies under CUSMA. Sure As Ship sends them with each U.S. quote and shipment and keeps them per product. A question you leave blank is not sent
  • New: While a product is marked as any of those regulated kinds, the product editor says US customs may ask for more information and can hold the parcel until it is given. Booking is never blocked
  • New: Warnings Sure As Ship gives with a booking, such as that one with the products it concerns, are shown when you book, stay on the order screen and are added as order notes. They clear when the shipment is voided
  • Tweak: Each customs line also carries the product’s SKU and page link
  • Fix: Changing a product’s HS code, country of manufacture or U.S. customs details now changes the U.S. duty quoted at checkout right away, instead of up to 15 minutes later

2.0.12

  • Tweak: When U.S. duties can’t be estimated at checkout because a product has no HS tariff code, an admin notice says so, links each product to fix, and points to the default HS code setting. It clears once a U.S. quote estimates the duties
  • Tweak: When Sure As Ship refuses to book a U.S. shipment for a missing HS code, the error names the items in Sure As Ship’s own words and says where to add the HS code in WooCommerce

2.0.11

  • Fix: When the carrier won’t cancel a shipment’s pickup, Void Shipment says the pickup is still scheduled (so the driver may still come) and notes it on the order, instead of reporting success
  • Tweak: Test Connection warns when your store currency differs from your Sure As Ship billing currency (checkout would otherwise show no Sure As Ship rates), and the warning and admin notice say how to fix it: set the store currency, or switch the billing currency in Company settings before your first shipment
  • Tweak: When Sure As Ship suspends your account, the admin notice gives the reason in Sure As Ship’s own words (for overdue invoices, paying in full restores the account)

2.0.10

  • New: The order screen shows where each parcel is (Delivered, In transit, Out for delivery and so on) as Sure As Ship reports it, instead of always saying Booked
  • New: Carrier scans (what happened, where and when) are listed under each shipment, and a Refresh tracking button checks with the carrier now
  • Tweak: A service without tracking (Canada Post Small Packet) says so and offers no refresh
  • Fix: When the carrier hasn’t confirmed a void, Void Shipment says so (the label may still be live, so don’t use it) and notes it on the order, instead of reporting success

2.0.9

  • New: The carrier pickup window the carrier agreed to (fitted to its own collection hours) is shown on the order and noted when the shipment is booked
  • Tweak: Pickup notes and settings name the carrier: each carrier makes its own pickup visit and charges its own fee, once per pickup date from each address
  • Fix: When Sure As Ship cannot quote for your account (suspended, or BYOC-only with no carrier account set up), checkout shows your fallback rate instead of no rate at all, and an admin notice says why

2.0.8

  • New: When a booking costs more than the checkout quote because of a carrier pickup fee, the order note names the fee
  • Tweak: Carrier Pickup settings say Canada Post pickups are supported, that pickup fees are billed to you once per stop per day (never to customers), and which pickups are free
  • Tweak: Pickup time settings explain that each carrier fits your window to its own collection hours (Canada Post collects 12:00 to 16:00)

2.0.7

  • Fix: Cross-border checkout quotes are refreshed when the cart’s value or the store currency changes, so the prepaid duty is never quoted on an old cart value

2.0.6

  • New: Export declaration number field on the order screen for Canadian exports outside the US (CBSA CERS proof of report), sent with the booking
  • Fix: A refused booking now says what to fix (export declaration, customs description, currency or carrier account) instead of always blaming the address
  • Fix: Customs values are sent with their currency, so they are no longer read as the account’s billing currency
  • Fix: Amounts on the order screen (quotes, shipment cost, price breakdown) are shown in the currency your Sure As Ship account is billed in
  • Fix: Checkout checks the currency of every rate, and hides any rate that does not state one

2.0.5

  • Tweak: Customs item values are sent to Sure As Ship in cents

2.0.4

  • Fix: Canadian addresses are booked with the province their postal code belongs to, so an order with a mis-picked province is no longer refused at booking
  • Fix: a background booking that fails is listed in a notice on the WooCommerce and order screens, with the reason and a link to each order
  • Fix: a pickup window that closes before it opens is refused, and carrier pickup is switched off so bookings keep working
  • Fix: unticking “Enable Sure As Ship Shipping” now hides Sure As Ship at checkout
  • Fix: with “Tracking Email” off, tracking is also left out of the Processing and Completed emails
  • Fix: the order-screen rate dialog offers only your enabled carriers and includes prepaid US duties, matching checkout
  • Tweak: notices appear only on the Plugins, WooCommerce Settings and order screens, and the setup reminder can be dismissed

2.0.3

  • Privacy: cross-border checkout quotes send only the product details needed to estimate duties, never the customer’s name or street address

2.0.2

  • New: shipping to the United States is quoted with the prepaid US duties and taxes included, and labelled, so shoppers pay them instead of the store

2.0.1

  • Fix: shipping is now quoted to shoppers before tax. Stores that charge tax on shipping were charging GST/HST twice on the shipping line

2.0.0

  • New home: now published on WordPress.org as “sure-as-ship-for-woocommerce”. Activating it switches off an older copy installed from sureasship.com; settings carry over
  • Fix: every order-screen and settings button (Book, Void, Test Connection, returns, boxes, locations) did nothing because the admin script failed to load
  • Fix: the store-wide settings page was hidden in recent WooCommerce versions, leaving nowhere to enter an API key
  • Fix: label, QR code, return and customs document links now open; they previously failed with “Missing API key”
  • Fix: saving a shipping zone’s Sure As Ship method no longer erases your ship-from locations and boxes
  • Fix: orders placed at the fallback rate can now be booked with “Book with Sure As Ship”
  • Fix: choosing a different default ship-from location now sticks
  • Fix: common carrier box sizes are no longer saved as your own boxes just by opening the settings; they are offered unticked
  • Changed: auto-booking runs in the background and retries temporary failures, instead of slowing down checkout
  • Changed: checkout waits at most 12 seconds for rates, and briefly remembers an outage so shoppers are not kept waiting on every change
  • Changed: the fallback rate is only shown when Sure As Ship is unreachable, never for a destination or cart that cannot be shipped
  • Changed: default dimensions and weight are in inches and pounds (12x8x6 in, 0.5 lb) whatever your store units, matching the Shopify app. Stores using metric defaults should check this setting
  • Changed: products missing any dimension use the default box, matching the Shopify app
  • Changed: markup percentage is applied before the flat handling fee, matching the Shopify app, and rates are sorted by the price customers see
  • Changed: rates refresh as soon as carriers, boxes, delivery options or product dimensions change
  • Changed: the merchant’s cost is no longer included in the public cart data used by block checkout
  • New: customers get an email with their tracking number when a shipment is booked (can be turned off)
  • New: the cost Sure As Ship charged is shown on the order, with a note if it is higher than the checkout quote
  • New: Test Connection checks the key you typed, before saving, and shows the account name
  • New: rates are hidden, with a notice, when the store currency differs from your Sure As Ship billing currency
  • New: debug logging removes names, addresses, phone numbers and emails
  • New: uninstalling removes the plugin’s settings and cached data (orders keep their shipment history)
  • Accessibility: labelled form controls, a keyboard-operable booking dialog, and status announcements
  • Security: all output escaped, input sanitized, and document downloads checked against the order

1.8.9

  • Fix: a ship-from location saved without a country no longer falls back to the WordPress store’s base country at checkout, order booking, or re-quote
  • New: saving a ship-from location whose postal code doesn’t match its country now shows a clear warning

1.8.8

  • Fix: products without dimensions fall back to a 12x8x6 default box, matching the Shopify integration
  • Fix: every packed item’s weight is floored at 0.1 lb before rating

1.8.7

  • Fix: customs commodity lines carry each item’s own per-unit weight

1.8.6

  • Fix: the rate cache varies on the delivery company and city/state, not just the postal code
  • Fix: international orders no longer send an empty country of manufacture
  • Fix: free line items carry a $1 minimum customs value
  • Fix: the admin re-quote sends the same options as the booking

1.8.0

  • Fix: multi-box orders book as one multi-piece shipment
  • New: “Customer Pricing” setting

1.0.0

  • Initial release
